meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'sick' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('a patient') (as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
colloquial insult: ты больной? = are you crazy?

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лезть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'get down, climb off'.

examples.trans: Are you sick? Get down immediately!

examples.text: Пробежала вся в слезах? А куда она могла пойти?
examples.trans: She ran past all in tears? And where could she have gone?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
goes right before the word it negates

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

meanings.en: to stop, put an end to
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to stop', forming an aspectual pair with 'прекращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Stop it! We will have the flat.

examples.text: Да ну что вы, прекратите! Это жизнь.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, stop it! That's life.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'circus', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('farce, a ridiculous situation') (colloquial: цирк какой-то!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
винить кого в чём = blame someone for sth

examples.trans: He blames the weather for everything.

examples.text: Иван, перестань винить себя во всём!
examples.trans: Ivan, stop blaming yourself for everything!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: + genitive: ни копейки = not a penny
Secondary conversational sense ('...  = neither... nor') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ловка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'trick, ruse' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я понимаю, что это твоя уловка.
examples.trans: I understand that this is your trick.

examples.text: Я прекрасно понимаю, что это очередная твоя хитрая уловка.
examples.trans: I understand perfectly well that this is another clever trick of yours.

examples.text: Опытный шеф сразу разгадал нехитрую уловку Сеня и Феди.
examples.trans: The experienced chef immediately saw through Senya and Fedya's simple ruse.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hang oneself'.

examples.text: Хочешь вешаться — вешайся, мне всё равно.
examples.trans: You want to hang yourself — hang yourself, I do not care.
Do you want to hang yourself?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

постоять.gloss: to stand for a while; to wait

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to stand for a while', forming an aspectual pair with 'стоять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = Wait!') (said to stop someone leaving) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll stand here for a bit.

meanings.note: + past tense: 'чтобы свидетели были'
Secondary conversational sense ('in order to') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to like') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('guy, lad, young man') (informal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'сунуть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'shove, stuff'.

examples.trans: You shoved him into a noose.

examples.text: Куда ты умудрился засунуть мой любимый нож?
examples.trans: Where did you manage to shove my favorite knife?

examples.text: Он быстро засунул записку в карман куртки.
examples.trans: He quickly stuffed the note into his jacket pocket.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'noose', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: На любимом фартуке шефа случайно оторвалась верхняя петля.
examples.trans: The top loop on the chef's favorite apron accidentally tore off.

examples.text: Из-за этого огромного долга он сам засунул голову в петлю.
examples.trans: Because of this huge debt he put his own head into a noose.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'realistic'.
Secondary conversational sense ('really, for real') (colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Do you think that's really possible?
It's realistic to do that in a day.

examples.text: Я не шучу и реально сваливаю отсюда.
examples.trans: I am not joking and am seriously getting out of here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'веситься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hang oneself'.
